content.text: Created in response to the following exchange within FCREPO-1771:
thank you very much for this release.  I have not found any faults with the build thus far.
I have attempted to structure some acceptance tests for the build using
Beaker
.  Please see the following:
https://github.com/jrgriffiniii/fcrepo4-vagrant-base-box/tree/FCREPO-1771-jrgriffiniii-beaker
Using an extension of RSpec, Beaker permits me to validate the state of the Box after it has been built.  For example:

[...]
  describe file('/opt/apache-karaf-4.0.1') do
    it { should be_directory }
  end

  describe file('/opt/karaf') do
    it { should be_symlink }
  end
[...]
Should this approach to quality assurance seem appealing, I encourage you to clone the branch within the forked repository, and execute the following:
$ bundle exec rspec spec/acceptance/
By default, I am testing against the Atlas build (this is a proof of concept).  I can just as easily restructure this to build against the environment provisioned using the BASH scripts.

Further (and, I would argue, ideally) this could be restructured for a CI environment.  Assuming that TravisCI builds do not timeout when downloading the base Box, I would speculate that this could be attempted using a .travis.yml file alone.
Please let me know if this is useful.  Thank you again.
(Please see
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1771?focusedCommentId=45929&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-45929)

I believe that I have made a successful attempt to resolve this issue (however, this may likely lead to a larger conversation rather than resolving this outright).  For all interested parties, I implore you to please inform me of your thoughts on my approach in response to my pull request:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-vagrant/pull/29
In response to the comment made by
on GitHub:
@jrgriffiniii for posterity, can you try and get TravisCI set-up with this on your account, so we know for sure whether or not it is possible?
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-vagrant/pull/29#issuecomment-152843110)
Sorry for the delay.  Yes, I shall work to integrate this with TravisCI by tomorrow morning (at the latest).
Pending response to code review comments.
I like the looks of this... but have not succeeded in making it work. Please see comments in GitHub.
Pending response to code review comment.
Pending response to:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-vagrant/pull/29#issuecomment-187466513
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing.  It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.

Created in response to the following exchange within FCREPO-1771:

Nick Ruest thank you very much for this release. I have not found any faults with the build thus far.

I have attempted to structure some acceptance tests for the build using Beaker. Please see the following:

https://github.com/jrgriffiniii/fcrepo4-vagrant-base-box/tree/FCREPO-1771-jrgriffiniii-beaker

Using an extension of RSpec, Beaker permits me to validate the state of the Box after it has been built. For example:

[...]
  describe file('/opt/apache-karaf-4.0.1') do
    it { should be_directory }
  end

  describe file('/opt/karaf') do
    it { should be_symlink }
  end
[...]

Should this approach to quality assurance seem appealing, I encourage you to clone the branch within the forked repository, and execute the following:

$ bundle exec rspec spec/acceptance/

By default, I am testing against the Atlas build (this is a proof of concept). I can just as easily restructure this to build against the environment provisioned using the BASH scripts.

Further (and, I would argue, ideally) this could be restructured for a CI environment. Assuming that TravisCI builds do not timeout when downloading the base Box, I would speculate that this could be attempted using a .travis.yml file alone.

Please let me know if this is useful. Thank you again.

(Please see https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1771?focusedCommentId=45929&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-45929)

I believe that I have made a successful attempt to resolve this issue (however, this may likely lead to a larger conversation rather than resolving this outright). For all interested parties, I implore you to please inform me of your thoughts on my approach in response to my pull request:

https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-vagrant/pull/29

In response to the comment made by Nick Ruest on GitHub:

@jrgriffiniii for posterity, can you try and get TravisCI set-up with this on your account, so we know for sure whether or not it is possible?

(https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-vagrant/pull/29#issuecomment-152843110)

Sorry for the delay. Yes, I shall work to integrate this with TravisCI by tomorrow morning (at the latest).
I like the looks of this... but have not succeeded in making it work. Please see comments in GitHub.
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing. It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.
